assessment.rationale: No frontier model has been fully interpreted from neurons to goals, so the Main KPI of 1 frontier model fully interpreted is unmet. Anthropic's attribution-graph work on Claude 3.5 Haiku reports useful insight on roughly a quarter of prompts tried, using a replacement model that only partly captures the original (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2025/attribution-graphs/biology.html). Sparse autoencoders leave unexplained dark matter in activations that grows harder to remove with scale (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.14670). Complete end-to-end reverse engineering has been achieved only for toy networks such as one-layer group-operation models (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.06581). Strong open tooling exists: Gemma Scope 2 releases SAEs and transcoders for every layer of Gemma 3 models up to 27B (https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-scope-2-27b-it). Honest limit: full interpretation has no agreed completeness criterion, so the KPI needs a verifiable definition before any reward; tasks that rerun existing SAEs or circuit tracing on open models are known work.

additionalSearches.finding: Attribution graphs gave satisfying insight on about a quarter of prompts; graphs are simplifications via an incomplete replacement model.

additionalSearches.finding: SAEs leave dark matter; larger SAEs struggle on the same contexts as smaller ones (TMLR 2025).

additionalSearches.finding: Gemma Scope 2: open SAEs and transcoders for every layer of Gemma 3 270M to 27B; tools, not a full interpretation.

additionalSearches.query: fully reverse engineered neural network complete interpretability toy model only frontier model not achieved
additionalSearches.finding: Full reverse engineering reported only for toy settings (one-hidden-layer nets on S5/S6); no complete account of a frontier model.
